title: Thrall's Origin Story Was a Cancelled Cartoon Adventure Game
hook: Blizzard announced a point-and-click adventure starring Thrall in 1997 and cancelled it the next year, just before E3. Eighteen years later the whole game leaked online. Would you play it today?
script: Did you know Blizzard once built a point and click cartoon adventure game starring Thrall, and then threw the whole thing away? It was called Warcraft Adventures: Lord of the Clans, and Blizzard announced it in nineteen ninety seven. You played Thrall, an orc raised as a slave by a human lord, who escapes and sets out to reunite the scattered orc clans. The hand drawn animation came from a Russian studio called Animation Magic. The game was nearly finished, with voice acting recorded and cinematics done. Then, the following May, just before E3, Blizzard cancelled the whole project. Blizzard's Bill Roper later admitted it would have been great three years earlier. The company insisted the call was about quality, not money, and not a verdict on adventure games. But Thrall himself survived the cancellation. His story was retold a few years later in a novel by Christie Golden. Then he went on to lead the Horde in Warcraft Three and World of Warcraft. Then in two thousand sixteen, eighteen years after the cancellation, a near complete playable build leaked online, cinematics and all. Blizzard's lost game could finally be played. Would you play a cartoon Warcraft adventure today? Follow for more gaming history.
